title: Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Deviation Settlement Mechanism and Related Matters) Regulations, 2024

impact.market_note: Deviation is priced off the market: the normal rate is the highest of the DAM price, the RTM price, or a blend that includes ancillary service cost. Wind and solar sellers settle at their own contract rate without frequency linkage, inside bands that tightened from 01.04.2026 to 5% for solar and hybrids and 10% for wind.

key_points.text: Normal rate = highest of the weighted average DAM price, RTM price, or one third each of DAM, RTM and the ancillary service charge
Wind and solar: under-injection beyond the outer band costs 200% of contract rate; over-injection beyond it earns nothing
From 01.04.2026 the inner band is 5% for solar and hybrids and 10% for wind; the denominator moves to X% of available capacity plus (100-X)% of schedule, X set by separate order
Pool deficits are recovered from drawee DICs: 50% on drawal and 50% on GNA to 31.03.2026, then by each DIC's reserve shortfall
Deviation charges are payable within 10 days; a defaulter must open an LC of 110% of its average payable

procurement.text: Each generator and ESS at a shared interconnection point needs its own Special Energy Meter
Aggregation at a pooling station through a QCA settles at the weighted average contract rate; de-pooling is by agreement
Sellers cleared in HP-DAM: under-injection on that quantum is priced at the HP-DAM price

discoms.comment: States as buyers pay over-drawal at up to 200% of the market-linked normal rate beyond the outer volume limit; RE-rich and RE super-rich states get wider limits (200 MW and 250 MW inner).

re_developers.comment: Deviation is settled at contract rate without frequency linkage; beyond the outer band under-injection costs 200% of contract rate and over-injection earns nothing. From 01.04.2026 the inner band is 5% for solar and hybrids, 10% for wind.

storage.comment: Standalone ESS settles like a general seller, with over-drawal while charging treated as under-injection; pumped-storage charging follows the solar rules for the initial period.

conventional.comment: General sellers settle at their reference charge rate with frequency linkage: beyond 10% or 100 MW, under-injection pays up to 200% of RR below 49.90 Hz, and over-injection earns nothing below 50.10 Hz.

transmission.comment: RLDCs and RPCs run weekly deviation accounts and the pool; NLDC frames the deficit-recovery procedure and the reserve-shortfall method.

traders.comment: Because the normal rate tracks DAM and RTM prices, deviation cost moves with exchange prices; HP-DAM sellers' under-injection is priced at the HP-DAM price.

open_questions: The value of X in the post-01.04.2026 formula for wind and solar is set by a separate CERC order; check the one in force.
CERC has since deferred reserve-shortfall based deficit recovery (to 05.04.2027 by a later order); this reads the 2024 text as notified.

title: RERC (Terms and Conditions for Green Energy Open Access) Regulations, 2025

impact.market_note: Rajasthan opens green open access from 100 kW of contract demand (no floor for captive). New captive RE can go up to 200% of contract demand if 20% of the extra energy is stored in BESS. New STU-connected RE above 5 MW must add 2-hour storage of at least 5% of capacity, and storage earns transmission and wheeling charge exemptions.

key_points.text: Eligibility from 100 kW of contract demand, aggregated within an electricity division; no lower limit for captive use
New captive RE up to 200% of contract demand; capacity above 100% must store at least 20% of its energy in BESS, operated as SLDC or the discom directs
BESS supplying in peak or non-solar hours: 75% T&W exemption at 5% storage, +1% per extra 1% up to 30%, 100% above 30%, for seven years, capped at 2,000 MW or 2030

Banking up to 100% of contract demand: annual, capped at the higher of 25% of injection or 30% of consumption; from 100% to 200%: within the billing cycle, 30% cap; 8% charge in kind; none for third-party sale or behind-the-meter
Generators with a discom PPA cannot take open access for that capacity except under the PPA

procurement.text: BESS for at least 20% of the energy from captive capacity above 100% of contract demand
New STU-connected RE over 5 MW (excluding hydro): ESS of at least 2 hours for at least 5% of RE capacity
ABT-compliant 15-minute Special Energy Meters at generator, interface and consumption points
Fees: Rs 1 lakh long-term, Rs 20,000 medium-term, Rs 5,000 short-term; bank guarantee of Rs 10,000/MW; three months' charges as deposit
Green tariff from the discom: requisitions for at least a year, in steps of 25%
Relinquishing long-term access early costs 66% of transmission and wheeling charges for the stranded period

discoms.comment: Sales to OA consumers from 100 kW are exposed, but cross-subsidy and additional surcharges, standby charges and the 8% banking charge stay; green energy bought above RPO counts towards the discom's RPO.

ci_consumers.comment: Consumers from 100 kW can source green power through OA or ask the discom for green tariff in 25% steps. They pay cross-subsidy and additional surcharge, and additional surcharge also applies to OA above contract demand.

captive.comment: New captive RE up to 200% of contract demand (BESS for 20% of the extra energy); no additional surcharge on captive supply; annual banking for plants up to 100% of contract demand.

re_developers.comment: Captive and OA demand opens up, but new STU-connected projects above 5 MW must add storage, and hybrid injection above contracted capacity is neither paid nor settled.

storage.comment: Demand from two mandates (20% storage for captive capacity above 100%, 5% two-hour ESS for new STU RE above 5 MW) and T&W exemptions of 75% to 100% for BESS supply in peak or non-solar hours.

transmission.comment: STU is the nodal agency for long and medium term, SLDC for short term; applications from the central portal are decided within 15 days, and system strengthening for RE is paid by the applicant.

open_questions: How BESS for 100% to 200% captive plants is operated is left to a separate SLDC or discom order.
The green energy tariff is to be set by a separate RERC order.
RERC's order of 04.11.2026 (Petition 2416/2026) reads the 200% limit as available to existing behind-the-meter plants only after migrating under Regulation 7.
